data.title: Spain's Pablo Hernández De Cos To Be Next ECB Chief
data.description:
BRUSSELS/FRANKFURT/PARIS (dpa-AFX) - Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos is set to succeed Christine Lagarde as the European Central Bank president when the latter steps down in February next year.

He would be the first Spaniard to be at the helm of the central bank for the single-currency bloc.

The euro area member states agreed to recommend de Cos as the ECB chief and France's Laurence Boone and Germany's Markus Brunnermeier as ECB Executive Board members, European Council President António Costa said in a post on the social media platform X on Thursday.

The former Bank of Spain governor's appointment to the top post of one of the major central banks in the world, awaits formal approval following a European Council meeting in December. His only rival in the race to be the ECB chief was the former Dutch central bank governor Klass Knot.

The Spanish economist has been the general manager at the Basel, Switzerland-based Bank of International Settlements since July 2025. He was the governor of the Bank of Spain, an institution he served since 1997, and a member of the ECB Governing Council from 2018 to 2024.

Late October, the current ECB President Lagarde announced her decision to step down from her post on February 07, 2027, roughly nine months ahead of the expiry of her eight-year term. She is leaving the job in search of a larger freedom to express her political views.

Brunnermeier is set to replace Philip Lane as the ECB chief economist and Boone will replace Isabel Schnabel who is now in charge of the market operations, when their terms end in May and January, respectively.

De Cos, with a strong background in monetary policy and central banking, is widely known to be moderately dovish in his stance as shown by his actions in the past. His appointment comes at a crucial time for the Eurozone economy as it battles high inflation that is much beyond the 2 percent target and turmoil in the debt market due to rising bond yields, in particular for France.

The ECB is widely expected to raise interest rates further in December as inflation hit a three-year high of 4.0 percent in October and is expected to remain strong in November driven by surging energy prices.

data.title: Peter Marrone Announces Acquisition Of Securities Of Sendero Resources Corp.
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

    Toronto, Ontario – TheNewswire - November 26, 2026 – Peter Marrone (the “Acquiror”) announces that he has acquired 1,415,094 units (the “Units”) of Sendero Resources Corp. (“Sendero”) pursuant to its non-brokered private placement completed on November 24, 2026, at a price of $0.53 per Unit for aggregate consideration of $749,999.82.

    Each Unit consists of one common share of Sendero (a “Common Share”) and one common share purchase warrant (a “Warrant”). Each Warrant entitles the holder to acquire one additional Common Share at a price of $0.70 until November 24, 2029.

    Following the acquisition, the Acquiror holds 3,572,060 Common Shares and 3,081,760 Warrants, representing approximately 11.60% of Sendero's issued and outstanding Common Shares on an undiluted basis and 19.64% on a partially diluted basis.

    The securities were acquired for investment purposes. The Acquiror may, depending on market conditions and other relevant circumstances, acquire additional securities of Sendero or dispose of securities held by him from time to time.

data.title: MINILUXE REPORTS THIRD QUARTER AND YEAR-TO-DATE FINANCIAL RESULTS FOR THE 13 AND 39 WEEKS ENDED SEPTEMBER 27, 2026
data.description:
Net Revenue Up 6% in the Third Quarter; System Sales Exceed $8M in a Quarter; Company Makes Multiple Growth Investments in Q3, Including New Studio Opening and Acquisition

All reported figures in U.S. Dollars unless otherwise noted

Boston, MA, Nov. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- MiniLuxe Holding Corp. today announced its financial results for the 13 weeks and 39 weeks ended September 27, 2026 (“Q3 2026” and “YTD 2026”, respectively). The comparative prior year periods are the 13 weeks and 39 weeks ended September 28, 2025.

MiniLuxe is on a mission to make self-care something you can feel good about, starting with your nails. The Company delivers premium nail care in studios known for hospital-grade hygiene, cleaner polishes, and treatments that are better for you and for the people who provide them. What sets MiniLuxe apart is its people and culture, which are at the center of its competitive advantage. In an industry infamous for churn and poor working conditions, MiniLuxe has retained 86% of its hourly workforce on average over each of the last three years. Team members who are with the Company five years or more receive stock options, giving them a stake in the Company’s success, along with real career paths. Today, more than half of MiniLuxe’s service professionals (nail designers and waxing specialists) have reached that milestone.

The third quarter of 2026 delivered another quarter of year-over-year growth, with total Company net revenue up 6.1% to $7.7M and system sales up 8% to $8.1M from $7.5M in Q3 2025. Growth was driven by continued same-studio sales gains in both volume and mix. System sales include sales from all MiniLuxe studios, including franchised locations. The quarter extends a long, unbroken run of year-over-year revenue growth, reflecting continued demand for MiniLuxe services.

The Company made multiple growth investments in the third quarter: new studios, new AI-driven, geo-targeted paid marketing tests, upgrades to existing studios, and additional nail designer hours ahead of the fourth-quarter holiday season, its period of peak demand. While these initiatives resulted in some short-term margin pullback, management expects them to deliver meaningful returns over the longer term. After the quarter ended, the Company also put in place its first price increase in approximately three years, of approximately 5%, which management expects to more than offset rising labor and health care benefit costs.

  • New studios: The Company opened its Mansfield, Massachusetts joint-venture studio on July 30 and acquired a majority interest in an existing studio in Burlington, Massachusetts on September 4. The third quarter was also the first full quarter for the new MiniLuxe Lakewood studio in Dallas.
  • Marketing tests: Early results are encouraging, with some test studios attracting record numbers of new clients who are also returning faster for repeat visits.
  • Studio upgrades: The Company began renovating several existing studios with new dual stations that allow a manicure and pedicure at the same time. In the first studios, these stations cost at least 50% less than legacy stations, and productivity per station has been as much as double that of legacy pedicure stations.
  • Nail designer hours: Staffed hours were up 7% over the prior year, which positions the Company well for fourth-quarter demand.

MiniLuxe’s Focus and Key Strategic Pillars in Q3 2026

The Company continued to make meaningful progress across each of its core strategic pillars in the third quarter of fiscal 2026:

  • Attract, develop and retain high-quality nail designer talent;
  • Drive growth through operating partners and franchise partners;
  • Accelerate overall studio-level profitability and drive overall Company profitability;
  • Strengthen balance sheet with sufficient capital to execute against growth plans.

Highlights of Business Performance

  • Total Company net revenue grew 6.1% to $7.7M in Q3 2026 from $7.3M in Q3 2025, bringing year-to-date revenue to $21.8M, up 4.3% from $20.9M in YTD 2025.
 Q3 2025Q3 2026ChangeYTD Q3 2025YTD Q3 2026Change
System sales$7.5M$8.1M+8%$21.4M$22.8M+7%
Net revenue$7.26M$7.70M+6.1%$20.87M$21.78M+4.3%
  • System sales grew 8% to $8.1M in Q3 2026 from $7.5M in Q3 2025, and 7% to $22.8M in YTD 2026 from $21.4M in YTD 2025. Net revenue grew 6.1% to $7.70M in Q3 2026 from $7.26M in Q3 2025, and 4.3% to $21.78M in YTD 2026 from $20.87M in YTD 2025.
  • General and administrative expense was $3.82M in Q3 2026 versus $3.60M in Q3 2025, an increase of 6.0%, primarily reflecting spend toward growth initiatives, including marketing tests and new studio openings. As a percentage of net revenue, G&A was flat year over year at approximately 49.6%. Year to date, G&A was $11.10M versus $10.90M in YTD 2025, up 1.9%, and declined to 51.0% of net revenue from 52.2%.
  • Operating loss was ($1.59M) in Q3 2026 versus ($1.26M) in Q3 2025, reflecting the growth investments described above; YTD operating loss was essentially flat at ($4.47M) versus ($4.45M) in YTD 2025.
  • Full Company Adjusted EBITDA was ($1.57M) in Q3 2026 versus ($0.89M) in Q3 2025, and ($4.23M) for YTD 2026 versus ($3.34M) for YTD 2025. Most of the change was driven by the timing of expenses and one-time items. Excluding one-time items, management estimates Normalized Adjusted EBITDA of ($1.27M) in the quarter, compared with ($1.02M) in Q3 2025.
  • During the third quarter, the Company issued 1,428,571 Class A Subordinate Voting Shares at a deemed price of $0.35 per share in settlement of a $500,000 third-party obligation (the gift-card holdback from the Paintbox acquisition).
  • At the end of Q3 2026 (September 27, 2026), cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash were $4.5M (Q2 2026: $6.1M; year-end 2025: $4.5M), and working capital was positive at $0.2M.

The Company continued to expand through operating partners and franchise partners. Overall gross franchise sales were up 53% in the third quarter and 102% year to date. The Mansfield, Massachusetts joint-venture studio opened on July 30, 2026, the Lakewood (Dallas) studio reopened as a MiniLuxe studio on June 5, 2026, and the Burlington, Massachusetts studio, acquired September 4, 2026, is operated through a 51%-owned limited liability company with its existing owner as operating partner.

Management Commentary

“In Q3, we continued to grow revenue year over year and expanded our studio footprint, with new studio openings and new locations in development. We also increased total nail designer hours and put marketing tests in place to attract new customers. We are already seeing early results as we attract new customers and see repeat visits, and we believe these investments will deliver a significant return over the medium to longer term. One of the most noteworthy statistics for me is that about half of our customer base is now Gen Z, which bodes well for the longevity of our brand and customer lifetime value.” – Tony Tjan, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer

Other Developments

  • Substantial Issuer Bid (SIB). The Company’s SIB for up to C$6.0 million of its Class A Subordinate Voting Shares expired at 5:00 p.m. (Toronto time) on September 24, 2026. No Subordinate Voting Shares were purchased under the offer and all tendered shares were returned to shareholders.
  • Paintbox New York studio. On September 7, 2026, the Company closed its “store-in-store” Paintbox studio in New York, New York. The Company had a short-term arrangement with a hair studio to use its space as a “store-in-store” concept, and the arrangement was not extended.
  • Acquisition of Belle Vista Nail Studio. On September 4, 2026, the Company formed MNLX Burlington JV LLC and acquired the assets of Belle Vista Nail Studio in Burlington, Massachusetts for cash consideration of approximately $0.3M, issuing a 49% interest in the new company to the sellers. MiniLuxe will convert this studio to its own brand in 2027.

The Company continues to evaluate accretive M&A opportunities and is in discussions with several nail studio operators that it believes fit its purpose of empowering nail designers, and where it can create shared value by applying MiniLuxe’s brand standards and back-office infrastructure.

Non-IFRS Measures and Reconciliation of Non-IFRS Measures

This press release references certain non-IFRS measures used by management. These measures are not recognized under International Financial Reporting Standards (“IFRS”), do not have a standardized meaning prescribed by IFRS, and are therefore unlikely to be comparable to similar measures presented by other companies. Rather, these measures are provided as additional information to complement those IFRS measures by providing further understanding of the Company’s results of operations from management’s perspective. Accordingly, these measures should not be considered in isolation nor as a substitute for analysis of the Company’s financial information reported under IFRS. The non-IFRS measures referred to in this press release are “Adjusted EBITDA”, “Normalized Adjusted EBITDA”, and system sales.

Adjusted EBITDA

Management believes Adjusted EBITDA most accurately reflects the commercial reality of the Company’s operations on an ongoing basis by adding back non-cash expenses. Additionally, the rent-related adjustments ensure that studio-related expenses align with revenue generated over the corresponding time periods.

Adjusted EBITDA is calculated by adding back fixed asset depreciation, right-of-use asset amortization under IFRS 16, asset disposal, and share-based compensation expense to IFRS operating income, then deducting cash rent expenses net of lease abatements. When relevant, we will add back adjustments made to the P&L as a result of accounting policies that are non-cash or do not have operational impacts (for example, inventory adjustments or deferred revenue). IFRS operating income is revenue less cost of sales (gross profit), additionally adjusted for general and administrative expenses, and depreciation and amortization expenses. Normalized Adjusted EBITDA is calculated as Adjusted EBITDA, further adjusted to (i) remove items that management considers one-time or not representative of ongoing operations, and (ii) present the comparative period on a basis consistent with the current period. Management uses Normalized Adjusted EBITDA to assess the Company’s run-rate operating performance. It should be read together with, and not as a substitute for, operating loss and Adjusted EBITDA.

About MiniLuxe

MiniLuxe Holding Corp. is a Boston-based lifestyle brand and talent empowerment platform transforming the fragmented beauty and self-care industry through its premium service brand, proprietary products, and operating platform. For more than 15 years, MiniLuxe has delivered high-quality nail care, waxing, and esthetic services through a growing network of company-owned, joint venture, and partner-operated studios, completing more than 5 million services to date.

The Company is recognized for its elevated service experience, rigorous hygiene standards, non-toxic products, modern studio design, and commitment to socially responsible labor practices. MiniLuxe’s differentiated model is designed to create better outcomes for both clients and beauty professionals through career development, economic mobility, equity participation, and future ownership opportunities.

MiniLuxe is expanding its reach through a multi-pronged growth strategy that includes new studio development, franchising, and the acquisition and conversion of existing nail studios. By combining a trusted consumer brand, proprietary products, operating expertise, and technology-enabled systems, the Company offers entrepreneurs and operators the opportunity to partner with a proven platform while preserving a strong focus on talent development and service excellence.

Through its growing studio network and product portfolio, MiniLuxe seeks to build the leading trusted brand in beauty and self-care while generating long-term value for clients, talent, and shareholders.
